declarations.documentation:
The image-model capability — provided at the root by `use imagegen.provider(...)`. It hands back the
whole `connection`, not just the key: the model id is the provider's CONFIGURATION (an argument of
`provider`, held in its handler state), not a capability of its own, so a call learns what it is
calling and as whom in ONE request instead of two. The credential half is resolved per call, so an env
rotation or an oauth refresh lands without a restart.

declarations.checkedType: agent(context: string, parts: array[unknown]) -> unknown with credential | throw[api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
POST a generateContent turn whose user @parts@ are the caller's, and hand back the reply's parsed
document — the ONE wire call both tools make (same endpoint, same api-key header), so only the parts
differ between generating and editing.

A non-2xx arrives here as the transport's `http.status_error` and leaves as `http.api_failure`,
classified by the stdlib's `http.classify_status`: this is the one boundary where the status is read,
and above it no caller sees a bare status again. A 401 or 403 becomes `http.auth_error` — the Gemini
key is wrong, revoked, or not entitled to the image model, and a `replay` converter turns that into a
fresh resolution of the credential (and, when it cannot be refreshed, the runtime's re-authorization
park). Every other non-2xx becomes `http.api_error` — a rejected prompt, a rate limit, a model name
that does not exist — carrying the server's body verbatim, because it is the diagnosis a model reads
and adjusts to, and the STATUS onward, so a retry policy downstream reads a number. @context@ names
the call ("image edit", "image generation") on whichever variant comes out. A transport failure
(`http.fetch_error`) and a 2xx that is not JSON (`json.parse_error`) are NOT statuses to classify, so
the residual rethrows them as bound.
declarations.name: generate_content

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

declarations.signature: agent generate_content(parts: array[unknown], context: string) -> unknown

declarations.checkedType: agent(context: string, parts: array[unknown]) -> file with credential | throw[no_image | malformed_base64 | api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
The whole shared shape of both tools: make the generateContent call with the caller's @parts@, then
hand back the reply's first image as a `file`. What is left in each tool above it is exactly the parts
it builds — everything else (the endpoint, the header, the classification, the read of the reply) is
written once here.

A reply that carries no image part is the typed `no_image`, carrying whatever text the model sent
instead (a refusal, a clarification) — never a panic. @context@ names the call ("image edit",
"image generation") in every message this path can produce.
declarations.name: generated_image

declarations.signature: agent generated_image(parts: array[unknown], context: string) -> file

declarations.checkedType: agent(image: file, instruction: string) -> file with credential | throw[no_image | gone | malformed_base64 | api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
Tool: edit an image with an instruction (e.g. "make the sky a sunset", "remove the text").
Pass the image's handle object — a bare {"$katari_ref": "<id>"} suffices; the result is a new image
file, whose handle you can pass to any of your tools that take a file — to look at it, or to post it.
A reply without an image throws the typed `no_image` carrying the model's text.
declarations.name: edit_image
